stories.title: ecoLogicStudio integrates microbes into building design
stories.summary: ecoLogicStudio uses algae, fungi and cyanobacteria to filter air and store carbon in its installations. The London practice says these organisms allow buildings to move beyond conventional construction and become active participants in environmental processes. A forest is a system, and the studio is building one.

stories.title: Climate tech innovations on the Great Barrier Reef
stories.summary: Sophia Hamblin Wang is using carbon-capture technology to address climate change in Far North Queensland. Following the destruction caused by cyclone Larry in 2006, Wang and other volunteers are working to protect the reef. The region is now looking for solutions to its increasingly abundant weather.

stories.title: Bihar Green Conclave 2026 discusses sustainable urban growth
stories.summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry and the Indian Green Building Council held the 4th Bihar Green Conclave in Patna. The event focused on green buildings and climate-resilient infrastructure under the theme of a green trillion. The state is currently planning 12 satellite townships to advance urban growth.

stories.title: India targets net zero emissions by 2070
stories.summary: India is aiming for net zero emissions by 2070, with a focus on energy-efficient construction and low-carbon materials. The transition requires collaboration between policymakers, developers and technology providers to manage rapid urbanisation. The building sector is expected to play a central role in the national economic transformation.

stories.title: CityUHK develops infrared-transparent aerogel for cooling
stories.summary: Researchers at City University of Hong Kong have created a white infrared-transparent aerogel designed to improve passive cooling by up to 5.2 degrees Celsius. The team says the material addresses rising energy consumption from air conditioning. The study was conducted in collaboration with Xi’an Jiaotong University.

stories.title: Green office leasing in India expected to exceed 80 percent
stories.summary: Colliers India reports that sustainable office leasing across seven major cities is projected to reach 80 to 85 percent of the total market in 2026. The share of green office space has risen from 74 percent in 2023. Sustainability certifications are becoming a standard corporate preference.

stories.title: Eco-friendly offices become new corporate preference, green leasing to cross 80% in 2026: Report
stories.summary: Eco-friendly office spaces are becoming the preferred choice for companies in India, with their share in total office leasing across the country's top seven cities expected to cross 80 per cent in 2026, as businesses increasingly focus on sustainability and energy efficiency, according to a

stories.title: Victoria approves 15-storey mass-timber office tower
stories.summary: The Victorian Department of Transport and Planning has approved a 15-storey mass-timber office tower in Cremorne. Despite local council objections, the project is being billed as Australia’s tallest timber commercial building. The development will provide over 13,000 square metres of net lettable space.

stories.title: One Kochi hotel blends traditional Kerala architecture
stories.summary: Studio TAB designed the One Kochi hotel using a mix of traditional Kerala house layouts and colonial verandahs. The 25,000-square-foot property aims to provide a space akin to a family home. The design incorporates local craft techniques and elements of tropical modernism to define its aesthetic.

stories.title: Thiruvananthapuram assesses non-functional smart city projects
stories.summary: The Thiruvananthapuram city corporation is auditing 81 projects completed under the Smart City Mission. Launched in 2016 with a 1,538 crore rupee budget, many facilities remain underutilised or non-functional. The new administration has decided to restart the handover process for the projects.

stories.title: Chandigarh architecture exhibition highlights modernist legacy
stories.summary: The M N Sharma Architectural Society is hosting an exhibition featuring 38 photographs of Chandigarh. The display explores the city’s geometric layouts and modernist buildings. Organisers describe the city as an architectural vision brought to life through its planned sectors and iconic structures.

stories.title: Supreme Court permits conveyance deeds for Parsvnath projects
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has allowed the execution of conveyance deeds for allottees in completed projects by Parsvnath Developers. The court also partially relaxed a freeze on the firm's bank accounts to cover electricity and employee costs. The company is currently undergoing insolvency proceedings.

stories.title: Dayavanti Associates expands infrastructure services in India
stories.summary: Dayavanti Associates is applying Building Information Modeling and digital twin technology to Indian infrastructure projects. The firm says its approach helps clients reduce costs and improve delivery precision. It claims experience on projects valued at 2,000 crore rupees using UK-qualified professionals.

stories.title: Three Indian design practices explore facade innovation
stories.summary: Three design firms are using parametric screens and weather-responsive materials to manage building exteriors. AR13 designed a protective shield for a wellness studio in Gujarat to mitigate coastal climate and traffic noise. The design approach focuses on how structures respond to their immediate surroundings.

stories.title: Mahindra Lifespaces signs 100-acre plotted development in MMR
stories.summary: Mahindra Lifespace Developers has signed a 100-acre plotted development project on the Karjat-Murbad Road in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. This marks the company's first plotted project outside of Chennai. The developer plans to launch the site during the next financial year.

stories.title: ZM Digitech integrates building safety and management systems
stories.summary: ZM Digitech Communications is marketing end-to-end integration for fire safety, electronic security and building management systems. The company says it aims to bridge the gap between disconnected systems in commercial and industrial facilities. It has been operating in the sector for two decades.

stories.title: Agartala residents receive housing after eight-year wait
stories.summary: A total of 278 families living in a slum along the Haora river in Agartala have received flats under the state's affordable housing scheme. The beneficiaries waited eight years for the homes, which are part of a larger project estimated to cost INR 162.50 crore.

stories.title: 4Space designs restaurant around Arabian horse anatomy
stories.summary: Design studio 4Space has completed Falwa, an Abu Dhabi restaurant located in the Royal Equestrian Art academy. The firm says it explored the physical and kinetic qualities of horses to create abstract depictions of the animal's skeletal structure throughout the dining space.

stories.title: Powerhouse Parramatta opens with $915m price tag
stories.summary: Powerhouse Parramatta opens this weekend, featuring a white lattice exoskeleton wrapping 30,000 square metres of space. The project has faced years of criticism from dissenters regarding its $915m cost and a perceived shift away from the museum's core business toward contemporary art and events.

stories.title: Salt brick arch dissolves in Jeju Island rainfall
stories.summary: Architecture studio stpmj built a small arch from rose-colored salt bricks on Jeju Island, knowing that local summer rainfall would eventually dissolve the structure. The project was designed to allow weather to act as the architect, gradually removing the masonry over several months.

stories.title: Polycarbonate panels shield Miami library from hurricanes
stories.summary: 89th Studio has designed a 24-hour automated library kiosk in North Miami wrapped in high-velocity polycarbonate paneling. The structure is built to withstand hurricanes while housing a modular lending library unit. The design utilizes an ambiguous steel frame to meet the project's resilience requirements.

stories.title: Competition seeks new life for La Pyramide tower
stories.summary: An ideas competition has revealed three winning proposals to reimagine La Pyramide in Abidjan, a 15-story brutalist tower vacant for decades. Once a symbol of post-independence optimism, the structure is now the subject of adaptive reuse plans intended to make the landmark habitable again.

stories.title: LionHeart creates video installation for Zaha Hadid Foundation
stories.summary: Artist LionHeart has produced an 11-minute video installation titled The Rebar Beneath for the Zaha Hadid Foundation. The work marks the tenth anniversary of the architect's death by using archive drawings and performance to examine the relationship between visible surfaces and underlying structural forms.

stories.title: Herzog & de Meuron to transform warehouse into Eames Institute
stories.summary: The Eames Institute has unveiled plans by Herzog & de Meuron to convert a 134,000-square-foot industrial warehouse in Novato, California, into a museum. The project is scheduled to open in 2030, transforming the mid-century campus into a cultural destination while retaining its original architectural features.

stories.title: Updated plans released for Eames Institute museum
stories.summary: Herzog & de Meuron, Field Operations, and EHDD have released updated designs for the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity in Novato, California. The project will convert a mid-century industrial campus into a public museum, with construction expected to begin in 2028 and completion targeted for 2030.

stories.title: SOM masterplans new Egyptian city with lagoon network
stories.summary: Architecture studio SOM has unveiled plans for Alam Al Roum, a new city stretching 7.2 kilometres along the Mediterranean coast in Egypt. The 20.6-square-kilometre masterplan features 22 kilometres of seawater-connected lagoons designed to weave through the built environment to support stormwater management.

stories.title: Albania experiences building boom under prime minister
stories.summary: Albania is undergoing a significant building boom, with the country's prime minister, Edi Rama, positioning architecture as a tool for social change. The prime minister, a former pro basketball player and artist, has attracted numerous high-profile international architects to work on projects in the capital, Tirana.

stories.title: Architectural history highlights environmental management
stories.summary: Architectural historian Reyner Banham argued that buildings are complex systems for environmental management rather than just physical containers. His work suggests that heating, cooling, and lighting are essential to habitable space, moving the focus of architecture beyond simple form and enclosure.

stories.title: Rockwool market projected to reach $36.20 billion by 2035
stories.summary: The global rockwool market is expected to reach $36.20 billion by 2035, growing at a 6.30% CAGR. Producers are currently transitioning to electric manufacturing processes to reduce emissions, driven by tighter fire and energy codes on the demand side and decarbonization goals on the supply side.

stories.title: Pre-painted aluminum market evolves with green demand
stories.summary: The global market for pre-painted aluminum sheets enters 2026 with more disciplined procurement and a diversified supply architecture. The sector is shaped by stringent environmental regulations and demand from the automotive and building industries for materials that offer corrosion resistance and longevity.

stories.title: Construction minerals market valued at $650 billion
stories.summary: The global construction minerals market, which supplies sand, gravel, and limestone, is valued at an estimated $650 billion as of 2025. The market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals and a more regionally diversified supply architecture, with over half of the volume concentrated in Asia-Pacific.

stories.title: Atherton Bikes teases 3D-printed titanium prototype
stories.summary: Atherton Bikes has teased a new prototype, the A.200.G, featuring a 3D-printed titanium and carbon construction. The downhill bike is designed with a gearbox, marking an update to the company's previous mountain bike offerings. Full details are available for subscribers.

stories.title: Construction robotics funding triples to $1.6 billion
stories.summary: Construction robotics companies have raised $1.6 billion through October 29, more than four times the amount recorded in all of 2025. Investors are betting that robots can address labor shortages as contractors struggle to find enough skilled workers to meet demand.

stories.title: 3D-printed color router improves low-light imaging
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a 3D-printed color router designed to improve image quality in low-light conditions. The technology aims to enhance sensor performance, with further details on the research and its potential applications published in the November 2026 issue of Photonics Spectra.

stories.title: Holcim acquires Burdett Group to expand Australian footprint
stories.summary: Holcim has acquired the Burdett Group to grow its aggregates and circular construction business in Australia. The company says the move aligns with its NextGen Growth 2030 strategy to invest in attractive markets. Burdett Group supplies recycled construction materials and sand in the Melbourne metropolitan growth area.

stories.title: Mass timber gains traction as construction costs climb
stories.summary: Developers are increasingly turning to mass timber as rising material costs and tariffs make traditional steel construction more expensive. Manufacturers in Spokane report that mass timber buildings are faster and cheaper to erect. Economic headwinds are currently driving the shift toward more cost-effective building strategies.

stories.title: Exeter University completes Passivhaus student housing
stories.summary: The University of Exeter and Bouygues UK have topped out two student accommodation blocks built to full Passivhaus standards. The project aims for very low operational energy demand and high thermal performance. It signals a growing trend of using Passivhaus designs for multi-storey campus buildings in the UK.

stories.title: Professor calls for more green space to combat urban heat
stories.summary: Professor John Kusimi has urged municipal authorities to encourage greener property development to mitigate flooding and rising urban temperatures. He notes that paving residential compounds and covering land with concrete reduces natural rainwater absorption. This practice increases surface runoff and puts significant pressure on existing drainage systems.

stories.title: Study tracks light pollution in Western Ghats
stories.summary: A new study examines how artificial light at night affects protected areas in Kerala’s Western Ghats. Researchers are investigating how illumination from human settlements, roads, and tourism facilities impacts wildlife navigation and predator-prey interactions. The study assesses the diffuse glow created when light scatters in the atmosphere.

stories.title: India’s buildings face energy and water efficiency gap
stories.summary: Two office buildings may offer identical amenities and rents while consuming vastly different amounts of electricity and water. Researchers note that these operational differences are rarely visible when properties are leased or valued. High consumption levels add to broader infrastructure strain beyond the individual property boundaries.

stories.title: Odisha govt transfers executive officer of Aska municipality after massive flooding
stories.summary: BERHAMPUR: The state government on Wednesday transferred executive officer (EO) of Aska municipality Rajesh Kumar Mohapatra. The urban area bore the brunt of the massive flood under impact of cyclone Arnab triggered rainfall. The transfer order was issued by the Housing and Urban Development department.

stories.title: Gurugram housing societies fail sewage treatment tests
stories.summary: The Haryana State Pollution Control Board found that sewage treatment plants at 11 of 16 inspected residential societies failed compliance tests. The board plans to shut down the non-compliant plants and impose environmental compensation. Inspections follow reports of untreated sewage entering local drains in north Gurugram.

stories.title: Energy efficiency remains low priority for J&K buildings
stories.summary: Buildings in Jammu and Kashmir consume nearly 50 percent of the region's total energy, compared to 35 percent nationally. Experts attribute this to harsh climates and inefficient design. Despite the high consumption, energy efficiency standards remain largely unknown to the public and are absent from building bye-laws.

stories.title: Delhi pollution report sparks construction ban confusion
stories.summary: A report citing an air quality index of 687 suggests a construction ban in Delhi from 5 to 20 November. The report does not identify the issuing authority or provide official documentation. The figures and the status of the restriction remain unconfirmed by any public agency.

stories.title: SWA designs modular toolkit for Houston streetscapes
stories.summary: Landscape studio SWA has created a modular system of shade structures, lighting, and planters to improve walkability in Houston. The project is part of the city's Public Realm Action Plan. The city aims to make urban streetscapes more comfortable and delightful for pedestrians through these retrofitted cooling elements.

stories.title: Appeals court allows NYC pied-à-terre tax to proceed
stories.summary: An appeals court ruled that New York City can move forward with a luxury second home tax. The court reversed a lower court order, finding that plaintiffs failed to show any actual harm from the rollout. The tax is expected to generate 500 million dollars for the city.

stories.title: Geospatial maps proposed to mitigate urban flooding
stories.summary: Geospatial risk maps are being positioned as a tool to prevent urban developments in flood-prone areas. Experts argue that integrating data across institutions is necessary to identify hazards and evaluate land suitability. The effectiveness of these maps depends on centralizing information currently distributed across various technological platforms.

stories.title: Lancaster transforms highway into urban boulevard
stories.summary: The city of Lancaster, California, invested 11.5 million dollars to convert nine blocks of a busy highway into a walkable, tree-lined streetscape. The redeveloped area now hosts 250 public and private enterprises. The project replaced a landscape previously known for its resemblance to alien planets.

stories.title: Book examines landscape architecture for climate adaptation
stories.summary: A new book by Harvard professor Charles Waldheim documents 60 built experiments by architect Kongjian Yu. The projects use wetlands and restored habitats to manage flooding and climate volatility. The work demonstrates how landscape architecture can integrate ecological functions into urban infrastructure to support both people and nature.

stories.title: Architect proposes floating platform for Florence
stories.summary: Architect Angelo Renna has proposed a demountable, seasonal floating platform for the Arno River in Florence. The modular structure features a circular perimeter of 39 trees. Designed for the Pescaia weir, the project aims to reimagine the relationship between the city and its river through an ecological intervention.

stories.title: Shackleton AI raises $5 million for construction agents
stories.summary: Shackleton AI has raised $5 million to automate construction management using AI agents. The company aims to integrate these agents into the construction process, though specific details on how the software functions or its current deployment status remain limited. The funding round was announced by Konsulteer.

stories.summary: The Chartered Institute of Building (CIOB) is strengthening its presence in China following formal recognition as a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO), alongside growing recognition of its professional qualifications. CIOB’s NGO status, sponsored by the Shanghai Association of Science and Technology, enables the institute to expand its

stories.title: Aformic secures $6.95 million for industrial robots
stories.summary: Aformic has raised $6.95 million in seed funding led by Veteran Ventures Capital. The company reports over $34 million in purchase orders and says its robots have traveled 186,000 miles in customer facilities. The capital will support international expansion and the development of its Qursor software.

stories.title: Qonic launches AI agents for BIM modeling
stories.summary: Qonic has introduced Qonic AI, a collection of agents integrated into its cloud-based BIM platform. Users can describe tasks in plain language to find, check, and update model data directly. The company also launched an MCP server to allow connections to external AI assistants.

stories.title: Kivo targets building maintenance with new platform
stories.summary: Lagos-based Kivotech Ltd has opened early access to Kivo, a platform designed to track building data from construction to maintenance. The software aims to replace informal communication methods like WhatsApp groups with a centralized record of equipment and service history for facility managers and contractors.

stories.summary: Dayavanti Associates Brings London Expertise to India’s Infrastructure through BIM & Digital Twins, with Team Experience on Rs. 2,000 Crore Projects VMPL New Delhi [India], November 5: The India-headquartered firm combines UK-qualified professionals, advanced construction technology and integrated project management to support cost efficiency, delivery

stories.title: Cleantech startup altM raises $10.3 million
stories.summary: Bengaluru-based altM has raised $10.3 million in a Series A funding round led by Rainmatter and Mela Ventures. The startup plans to use the capital to scale manufacturing and build a 1,000-tonne-per-year commercial facility by 2028. It is currently focused on converting revenues from its pilot plant.

stories.title: Wave energy and AI data center deal announced
stories.summary: Four firms have signed a three-year memorandum of understanding to demonstrate how wave energy can trigger automated payments for data center power. The announcement in Jaffa Port is a technology demonstration rather than a commercial contract. No pricing or specific data center partners were disclosed.

stories.summary: The University of Liverpool celebrates its new Liverpool School of Architecture (LSA) building today (5th November 2026) with an official opening ceremony led by Game of Thrones actor and architecture alumnus Anton Lesser.
